title: CORTICAL DYSPLASIA, COMPLEX, WITH OTHER BRAIN MALFORMATIONS 17

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations-17 (CDCBM17) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DMRTA2 gene (614804) on chromosome 1p32.3.

checks.claim: Complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations-17 (CDCBM17) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DMRTA2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Autozygosity mapping and exome sequencing identified a homozygous novel single base pair deletion, c.1197delT in DMRTA2
checks.explanation: Homozygous DMRTA2 loss-of-function variant is proposed as the cause of the cortical malformation disorder.

checks.claim: The DMRTA2 gene is located on chromosome 1p32.3.
checks.evidence_quote: DMRTA2 encodes doublesex and mab-3-related transcription factor a2
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location. It is accepted only as standard gene nomenclature restating the paper's gene.

paragraphs.text: Complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations-17 (CDCBM17) is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder that begins before birth. Its features include fronto-parietal pachygyria, agenesis of the corpus callosum, and progressive severe microcephaly (Urquhart et al., 2016).

paragraphs.text: Urquhart et al. (2016) studied 3 affected sibs from a consanguineous family with CDCBM17. Using autozygosity mapping and exome sequencing, they identified a novel homozygous 1-bp deletion in the DMRTA2 gene (c.1197delT). The deletion was predicted to cause a frameshift (Pro400LeufsTer33). The authors stated that data from murine and zebrafish knockout models were consistent with the variant causing the cortical phenotype. They suggested that loss of DMRTA2 function leads to a novel disorder of cortical development.
